analysis.title: ETD Rates Watch: Treasuries Muted; Fed Inflation Fears Build As Warsh Remarks Loom
key_insights: Asian equities fell on tech fears tied to Nvidia and Microsoft: Nikkei -2.42%, Kospi -3.59%, Taiwan -6%, while Hang Seng and China H shares rose about 0.5%. Nvidia reports quarterly results this week.
Treasury market was quiet: TY futures traded a 5+ tick range between 105-10 and 105-04+, with a number of block trades posted despite the narrow range.

Chinese October activity data was weaker than expected except the unemployment rate (5.2% to 5.1%). Retail sales and industrial production missed. UBS Economics attributes part of September's strength to front-loading and says underlying domestic growth momentum is weak. CSI 300 fell just over 1%.

St Louis Fed President Schmid (non-voter) listed four reasons inflation stays elevated: energy, rising durable goods prices, spillover from the AI infrastructure buildout, and rising healthcare costs. He said the labour market is not a cause and rejected the view that inflation is due to one-time supply shocks.

Fed Vice Chair Jefferson said higher energy prices are leading to persistent inflation and that inflation is the most important signal for policy. Jefferson and NY Fed's Williams are the two senior advisers to Chair Warsh, and both are openly discussing rising inflation risks.

The Fed debate has moved from whether to hike to the pace of hikes. Waller floated a 50bp hike, Logan suggested 25bp moves in Dec/Jan, Hammack and Collins (non-voter in December) prefer a gradual approach.
BoE Chief Economist Pill said the Bank has further to go on energy-cost risks and that current market pricing is not 'outrageous'. Markets price 100bp of BoE hikes over the next 12 months.
Cornwall Insight estimates UK business electricity costs will rise about 13% on average by the end of the decade, driven by network investment, renewable scheme costs and Sizewell C charges.
earnings_insights: Nvidia is due to report quarterly results this week (date not given in the note).
